# aibox

> Reproducible AI workspaces from one aibox.toml.

Version: v0.35.1

## Change log

aibox release history.

- [v0.35.1 — Yazi Markdown preview and refreshed tools](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-35-1/): Restores rendered Markdown previews and refreshes v0 base-image and addon tool versions.
- [v0.35.0 — period terminal themes and graphics toolchains](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-35-0/): Adds Borland, Norton, and Phosphor themes plus opt-in D2, Graphviz, Vega, Vega-Lite, and Mermaid build-time renderers.
- [v0.34.5 — consistent tmux window separators](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-34-5/): Restores PowerKit separator colors across all themes and makes visual regressions release-blocking.
- [v0.34.6 — restored host runtime builds](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-34-6/): Accepts PowerKit's expanded pinned renderer while retaining structural separator validation.
- [v0.34.7 — configurable Yazi previews](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-34-7/): Adds persistent line numbers and wrapping, explicit preview scrolling, and hierarchical tabular size reports.
- [v0.34.2 — accurate themes and reliable agent state](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-34-2/): Adds the theme gallery and chooser, aligns generated themes with their references, and fixes Codex and tmux attention state.
- [v0.34.3 — readable themes and restored terminal titles](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-34-3/): Repairs Yazi marks and PowerKit dividers across all themes, preserves active-pane emphasis, and restores terminal titles on exit.
- [v0.34.4 — warning-free Yazi pane toggles](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-34-4/): Updates the bundled pane-toggle plugin for Yazi's current ratio API.
- [v0.34.0 — agent-aware tmux and branded documentation](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-34-0/): Adds configurable agent lifecycle titles and moves the documentation site to the projectious.work Hugo brand theme.
- [v0.34.1 — coherent terminal themes](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-34-1/): Unifies configurable colors across the managed terminal toolchain, restores the theme gallery, and fixes Codex lifecycle and LaTeX builds.
- [v0.33.2 — runtime and processkit alignment](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-33-2/): Refreshes processkit and runtime metadata while reconciling tmux layout and theme switching work.
- [v0.33.0 — agent-aware terminal titles](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-33-0/): Adds configurable, terminal-neutral tmux titles and lifecycle attention signals for agent panes.
- [v0.33.1 — resilient runtime projections](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/changelog/release-v0-33-1/): Repairs generated harness startup, Yazi directory previews, and PowerKit window-tab spacing.

## Features

What aibox provides.


## Roadmap

The public aibox delivery roadmap.

- [v0.x](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/roadmap/v0/): Mature the current aibox line around dependable containers, addons, agent context, runtime diagnostics, and processkit integration.
- [v1.x](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/roadmap/v1/): Develop the next project-contract architecture while preserving reproducible, provider-neutral workspaces.

## Themes

Compare every aibox theme, its semantic palette, emphasis, tool support, and terminal appearance.

- [Theme chooser](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/themes/chooser/): Find themes by appearance, contrast, and required tool integration.
- [Tool support](https://projectious-work.github.io/aibox/v0.x/v0.35.1/themes/tool-support/): See how each supported terminal tool consumes the shared semantic theme.
